0.long_answer: Organic acidemias are a group of metabolic disorders that disrupt the normal breakdown of branched-chain amino acids such as isoleucine, leucine, and valine. These disorders lead to the accumulation of toxic acids in the blood and can result in a range of symptoms in newborns, including hypotonia (poor muscle tone), vomiting, metabolic acidosis, and lethargy. Among the organic acidemias, specific conditions like maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) are well recognized as metabolic causes of hypotonia in neonates because they impair the metabolism of branched-chain amino acids, leading to a buildup of harmful metabolites that affect neuromuscular function.
